newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Western Digital opens Singapore data plant.
newsitem.headline: Western Digital opens Singapore data plant.

text.p: U.S.-based Western Digital Corp (WD) announced on Wednesday it is opening its first plant worldwide to manufacture high-end hard disk drives in Singapore.
WD said the drives, based on SCSI (small computer system interface) technology, are designed for workstations, local area network (LAN) severs and multi-systems.
The company's existing facility in Singapore produces hard disk drives for desk top and mobile personal computers.

"The Singapore Tuas plant is part of the corporation's Enterprise Storage Group, formed in late 1994, to broaden WD's successful data storage business into the enterprise computing market," the company said in a statement.
A company official said the group's move into the enterprise sector is headed out of Rochester, Minnesota, where all research and development work will be done.

The company aims to spend up to US$35 million on the new Singapore plant by the year 2000 when it would be capable of producing 3 million drives annually. For now the plant can produce several hundred thousand units per quarter.
